stories.headline: Chennai Gold Rate Today, November 11, 2026: 22-Carat Gold Falls by ₹195 Per Gram
stories.text: Gold and silver prices in Chennai declined sharply on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, according to the Madras Jewellers and Diamond Traders Association. The price of 22-carat gold in Chennai decreased by ₹195 per gram to ₹13,015 on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, according to the Madras Jewellers and Diamond Traders Association. The price of one sovereign consisting of 8 grams of 22-carat gold fell to ₹1,04,120 in Chennai on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. The price of 18-carat gold in Chennai fell by ₹160 per gram to ₹10,650 on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, according to the Madras Jewellers and Diamond Traders Association. The price of 14-carat gold in Chennai declined by ₹155 per gram to ₹8,550 on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, according to the Madras Jewellers and Diamond Traders Association. Silver prices in Chennai decreased by ₹5 per gram to ₹200 on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, according to the Madras Jewellers and Diamond Traders Association. The price of one kilogram of silver in Chennai stands at ₹2,00,000 on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, according to the Madras Jewellers and Diamond Traders Association. On Wednesday, November 11, the price of gold in Chennai decreased by Rs 1,560 per sovereign. Following a decrease of Rs 195 per gram, gold is priced at Rs 1,04,120 per sovereign and Rs 13,015 per gram in Chennai. Silver prices in Chennai decreased to Rs 200 per gram or Rs 2,00,000 per kg on November 11. On November 10, silver was priced at Rs 205 per gram in Chennai. Gold prices in Chennai increased from Rs 93,600 per sovereign on November 11, 2025, to Rs 1,04,120 per sovereign on November 11, 2026.

stories.headline: Global gold price drop 2026: Yellow metal slips 6% in dollar terms, but top Indian gold ETFs still deliver 7.5% returns
stories.text: Global gold prices dropped by over 6% in 2026, with TradingView data showing a year-to-date return of -6.36% and trading around $4,045 per troy ounce on 11 November. A weaker Indian rupee against the US dollar cushions falling international gold prices by making imports more expensive, supporting domestic prices. Quantum Mutual Fund reported that gold ended 30 October at $3,875 per troy ounce, marking a monthly decline of about 6.87% and falling nearly 30% below January's record high. Top performing Indian gold ETFs delivered positive returns this year exceeding 7.5%, with 360 ONE Gold ETF yielding 7.54% and Choice Gold ETF yielding 6.68% as of 9 November. Quantum Mutual Fund stated that October's 6.87% correction was driven by rising oil prices, persistent inflation, tighter US monetary policy expectations, and elevated real bond yields. Quantum Mutual Fund reported that global gold ETFs saw cumulative net inflows of $1.2 billion through 23 October and aggregate holdings increased by about 10 tonnes in October. Quantum Mutual Fund stated that government debt, global economic uncertainty, and geopolitical tensions could continue to support gold demand, despite price corrections.

stories.headline: Gold, silver prices today, 11 Nov Wednesday: Check retail rates of 24K, 22K gold, 999 silver in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata
stories.text: International gold and silver prices increased on Wednesday, 11 November, following higher-than-expected US inflation data on Tuesday. Domestic spot gold rose to ₹ 1,42,010 per 10 grams, and domestic spot silver climbed to ₹ 1,86,660 per kg, according to Bullions.co.in. On the Multi Commodity Exchange, gold futures traded at ₹ 1,41,470, up ₹ 945 or 0.67%, and silver futures gained ₹ 3,369 or 1.85% to reach ₹ 1,85,945. Manav Modi from Motilal Oswal Financial Services stated that gold prices experienced renewed pressure due to inflation data and hawkish Federal Reserve commentary. October headline Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% month-on-month, exceeding the 0.3% estimate, and core Consumer Price Index increased 0.3%.
